top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a genuine conceptual advance: the magic-wavelength condition cancels the light shifts of the clock levels so that many atoms can be interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts. It has matured into independently verified agreement between clocks in several laboratories at the 10^-18 level, which is the theory-experiment and cross-laboratory robustness I look for. It opens a new regime of precision measurement (gravitational redshift over millimetres, tests of constant drift) that nobody foresaw. The allocation to Katori and Ye is clean, and the citation scope is tight: the lattice-clock concept and its realisation, not clocks in general. No award would withhold a mature, reproduced, fundamental achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I have no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye, although as an atomic theorist working on precision atomic structure I am close to this field and my long-time collaborator Anne L'Huillier is a 2023 laureate in a different area.
